# Releasing

Releases are cut by the [Release](../.github/workflows/release.yml) GitHub
Actions workflow, which is triggered manually.

## Before releasing

* Make sure CI is green on `master`.
* Pick the next version following [semver](https://semver.org/). While we are
  pre-1.0, breaking changes and new features bump the minor version, fixes bump
  the patch version.
* Check that the merged PRs are labeled. Release notes are generated by GitHub
  and grouped by label (see [.github/release.yml](../.github/release.yml)):
  * `breaking-change`: Breaking Changes
  * `kind/feature`: New features
  * anything else: Maintenance and bug fixing
  * `kind/dependencies`: excluded

## Cutting the release

Run the workflow from `master`, passing the version without the `v` prefix:

```bash
gh workflow run release.yml --ref master -f version=0.13.0
gh run watch
```

Alternatively, use "Run workflow" on the Release workflow page in the GitHub
Actions tab.

The workflow:

1. Creates and pushes the annotated tag `v<version>`.
2. Runs [GoReleaser](https://goreleaser.com/) with
   [.goreleaser.yml](../.goreleaser.yml), which builds the binaries for Linux,
   macOS and Windows, and publishes them to a GitHub release together with a
   `checksums.txt` file.

Versions with a pre-release suffix (e.g. `0.13.0-rc1`) are automatically marked
as pre-releases.

## If the release fails

The tag is pushed before GoReleaser runs, so a failed run leaves the tag
behind and a re-run fails because the tag already exists. Delete it first:

```bash
git push --delete origin v0.13.0
```
